name: Liberia
summary: Eleven red and white stripes with a single white star on a blue canton. Modelled on the US flag, it reflects Liberia's founding by the American Colonization Society as a home for freed African Americans.
origin: Liberia was founded in the 1820s by the American Colonization Society as a settlement for free Black Americans and formerly enslaved people. It declared independence on 26 July 1847.
A committee of women led by Susannah Lewis sewed the flag, which was adopted on 24 August 1847, now Flag Day.

symbols.name: Eleven stripes
symbols.description: Six red and five white horizontal stripes.
symbols.meaning: The eleven signatories of the Liberian Declaration of Independence.

symbols.name: Lone star
symbols.description: A white five-pointed star on the blue canton.
symbols.meaning: The first independent republic in Africa, a beacon of freedom.

history.label: Commonwealth of Liberia
history.note: Thirteen stripes with a white cross in the canton.

facts: Its 10:19 ratio matches the US flag.
Liberian flags of convenience on ships mean the design is flown on more of the world's merchant fleet than almost any other.
Malaysia's flag has a similar layout with fourteen stripes and a crescent.
clues: Red and white stripes with a single white star on a blue canton.
Its eleven stripes stand for the signers of a declaration of independence.
Modelled on the flag of the country whose freed citizens founded it.
